subject: R^2 in SEM for the general model

messages.author: aa98f52379da5c71
messages.subject: R^2 in SEM for the general model
parts:
Dear sr.,

I want to know how to get multiple R square. I only have the R square per item, but I  need for the general model. This is the comand that I put

sem.fit = sem(mymodel,estimator="MLR",data=datos)
summary(sem.fit, fit.measures=T, standardized=T, nd=3)
semPaths(sem.fit,whatLabels="std",layout="tree",edge.label.cex=0.9,rotation=2,nCharNodes=15,
         sizeLat=7,sizeMan=7,style="lisrel")


head(modificationindices(sem.fit)[order((modificationindices(sem.fit))$mi,decreasing=TRUE),],15)
lavInspect(sem.fit,"r2")

I hope you can help me as soon as possible,

Fiorella Solis

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: R^2 in SEM for the general model
parts:
Such a thing does not exist. R^2 refers to the explained variances of the DV in the model and not to the model as such. If you fit a multiple regression with latent variables, then you can calculate the unique contributions of each IV (these are the squared standardized betas) and R^2 minus the sum of the unique contributions is then what cannot be uniquely assigned to a particular IV.

messages.subject: Re: R^2 in SEM for the general model
parts: LISREL used to report an overall coefficient of determination for a model. This was a function of all of the R2's for all dependent variables. It was something like 1 - a product of (1 - R2) across all the dependent variables (been a while). I think LISREL stopped reporting it because it was so hard to make sense of it. One particularly high or low value could dramatically color the result.
